content.content:
Ussa-Rekh: "An Owing is a debt that a person works off in labour. I buy out the people held, one at a time. I pay for the next one with the crews' hire. I will tell you plainly when that stopped working. It stopped the year the berths that I bought for the crews began to cost me more than their hire. A crew that goes early leaves me the berth's price to carry. With that price unpaid I can buy out no more Owings. The person held on an estate stays held. I hold that a season agreed is a season worked. So do the estates. Heavy-Rope, just along the dock, can tell you what his crew asked of me. I refused it for the reason I have given."
Objective completed: Hear Ussa-Rekh on the dock at Soulrest, just along from Heavy-Rope.
Journal entry (The Broker's Mercy): Ussa-Rekh told me on the Soulrest docks that he freed these crews and that they work the season as agreed. content.text:
I finished the quest, The Broker's Mercy, and my journal now has no active objective, so I stopped.

- **Setup:** Never-Sold sent me to the Soulrest docks. Heavy-Rope's crew had asked to end their last season of hire early, and Ussa-Rekh had refused.
- **What I heard:** Heavy-Rope has berths waiting for his crew in Lilmoth. Ussa-Rekh says an early exit leaves him carrying the berth's price, and then he can't buy out the next person held.
- **What I did:** I sided with Ussa-Rekh, because it echoed what I'd learned with Rows-For-Another: the next person held pays. I talked Heavy-Rope round with the Speechcraft 30 option, so I didn't need to pay the 50 gold. The crew will work the season, and the Lilmoth berths are gone.

I gave my take with the end command. It covered the echo with my earlier choice, the thin topic menus, the persuade option appearing twice, and not learning what became of the crew.
